claim: VCO frequency-vs-VCTRL characterization of design/vco/vco_ring5.sch with the issue-#232 CLK buffer (design/clk-buf) attached to its CLK node and loaded by the provisional 1 pF characterization load of spec/decision-records/DR-008-clk-output-load-and-buffer-scope.md, at the same six VCTRL points and the same 45-point PVT grid as the unbuffered sim/vco campaign. It is the buffered half of a pair: the unbuffered half is sim/vco/records/20260904-163130-f3ae976.md, and the difference per (corner, VCTRL) point is the tuning-range shift caused by the buffer's input capacitance on the ring-side node. Measured design input only; it ratifies nothing.
spec_rows_note: spec/target-spec.md row 2 (output band -- the free-running frequency this sweep reaches at each VCTRL point) and row 5 (Kvco -- the slope that frequency-vs-VCTRL curve defines), the two rows this manifest's own claim names. Both are DRAFT and owed a sky130 re-derivation; this is measured input to that, not a ratification.
methodology_note: identical to sim/vco's (same DUT, open loop, same six VCTRL values, same transient, same `uic` startup kick and 60 ns settle, same simulator options -- none) except that design/clk-buf is attached at the VCO's CLK node and loads it with the 1 pF DR-008 characterization load; the measured node is the ring-side net `vcoclk` (the node the divider taps in design/top), NOT the buffered pin, so the sweep reads exactly the loading the buffer adds to the ring. Read it against the unbuffered baseline named in the claim, point for point; the shift is the figure, not either absolute frequency. The same dump-grid caveat as sim/vco's applies to the upper-half VCTRL rows, which is why a paired comparison on the same 50 ps grid is the right read.
analysis: transient per swept VCTRL value (`tran 50p 200n uic`, six values, one ngspice invocation per PVT point)
